$comment: Cross-client parity matrix. Both runners read this file verbatim and configure through the same ordered calls, so neither can drift from the other. Base parameters are buckley_case_a from src/lib/ressim/src/tests/buckley.rs. `strict` cases must agree to 1e-9; a non-strict case would report its gap instead of failing. Every case is strict since FIM-DIRECT-001 (docs/FIM_CROSS_TARGET_DIVERGENCE_2026-09-22.md section 9).

cases.why: The original fixture. Three steps leaves the front mid-grid; a fully swept or static field would agree without proving much.

The same case on the implicit solver. Strict since FIM-DIRECT-001: it used to take 18 substeps natively against 4 in wasm, because roundoff of one sign in the inactive two-phase gas unknown made every later Jacobian singular. Both targets now take 4 and agree to ~1e-13.
Mobility ratio is the axis the catalog's sensitivities vary most. A favourable displacement moves the front differently and exercises the relperm path at different saturations.
Adverse mobility on the implicit solver. Strict since FIM-DIRECT-001, for the same reason as buckley-fim; its former 1.24e-05 residual after backend unification was the same defect, not libm or SIMD.

A different cell count changes array sizes across the boundary, and grid refinement is a numerics sensitivity in its own right. Short step because 12 highly permeable cells sweep in well under a day, and parity measured on a uniform field proves nothing (front lands at 5 of 12).
